requests.question: How does the competition store INV-023, the 'Primary investigative question' entered when an investigation is started? Journey J1 (verification/journeys/bindings.json, all three P0) binds INV-023 in J1-03, checks the entered question in GitHub itself in J1-05 (providerHolds([problem, title, question]), j1-create-persist.spec.mjs) and on reload in J1-06. The pre-competition field map (docs/contract-readiness/causa-precompetition/UI-FIELD-MAP.json, UB-023) maps INV-023 to Payload.InvestigationDetailsRevised.question (CMD-INV-CREATE) and marks it blocked by OD-CR-01; causa-storage 1.1.0 (causa-data contract/v1.1.0/CONTRACT.md section 1; requirements-compiled/v4.1.6/proposals/STORAGE-1.1.md section 3) leaves InvestigationDetailsRevised to a later 1.2.0; and COMPETITION-CONSUMPTION.md (section 2) says a blocked binding stays unimplemented until the owner decides, and an agent must not choose the meaning of a blocked field itself. The frozen InvestigationStarted payload is exactly {title, observationId, original} (causa-data contract/v1.0.0 CONTRACT.md, unchanged in 1.1.0), so no 1.1.0 field of the start holds the question; the only wire field named question is UnknownIdentified {unknownId, question, materiality}.
options: A: for the competition, store INV-023 as one UnknownIdentified with materiality informational, written in the same command group as the start (CMD-INV-CREATE); on reload the earliest-created unknown is the primary question. Side effects: the question also appears in the unknowns list, and it needs a migration once causa-storage 1.2.0's InvestigationDetailsRevised exists
B: do not store it: J1-05 and J1-06 then fail on the question value and stay failed for the competition; J1-03's start is unaffected
requests.recommendation: A: it uses only fields the frozen 1.1.0 contract already has, keeps the entered question in GitHub where J1-05 and J1-06 look for it, and keeps the start a single command group; its cost (the question listed among the unknowns, a later migration to InvestigationDetailsRevised) is named here so it is the owner's choice, not an agent's reading of a blocked field.
requests.rationale: UB-023 is a blocked binding (OD-CR-01); COMPETITION-CONSUMPTION.md section 2 leaves its meaning to the owner.
requests.impact: With A the competition's CMD-INV-CREATE writes InvestigationStarted and one UnknownIdentified (materiality informational) together, and the workspace reads the earliest-created unknown as the primary question. With B J1-05 and J1-06 stay failed for the competition. P19 pins no file: the lock binds this request's text through ownerDecisionRequests.sha256 (launch-preflight LP-03).

requests.title: Approve the competition scope (successor of ODR-R10-01)
requests.question: Approve docs/competition-readiness/scope-manifest.json as the full scope of the 7 November competition, as shown below (requirements, obligations, work items, zero exclusions, scopeSha256)? It is compiled by `requirements-compiler scope compile` from the frozen v4.1.6 (tag indy-init-requirements-v4.1.6, manifest 8d3706d9...), its plan supplement (WDL-013 verified per obligation, ODR-V416-WDL013 A), the catalog ratified for v4.1.6 (ODR-V416-CAT) and the requirements baseline, with the fixed (V2) selectors (ODR-V416-SCOPE-SELECTORS A, SS-1 A): 209 requirements (162 plan incl. WDL-013, 47 catalog), 921 obligations (616 plan, 663 plan tests), 31 work items (4 generated: WI-GEN-VER and the three catalog screens), 358 gate-level requirements, scopeSha256 09e38f7d... Rehearsal 010's approved scope (26e6ff3c..., ODR-R10-01, APR-R10-OWNER-4) stays as it is, a historical record. Slice integration and full-release acceptance remain separate gates. Asked only once indy-init-requirements-v4.1.6 is tagged and the manifest is current (compiled from the package, supplement and catalog on main).
options: A: approve the competition scope as shown
B: do not approve (the scope is recompiled after changes)
requests.recommendation: A, after checking the counts and digest shown against the pull request that compiled it (`scope preflight` PASS; the offline suite reproduces it byte for byte and checks WDL-013's three obligations are bound and no WI-GEN-PF/UI/EXT-DATA/WDL item remains).
requests.rationale: The scope is approved once, by digest; any later change needs a new approval. SS-1 A: the competition scope is compiled with the fixed selectors and approved on its own digest.
requests.impact: The competition lock pins this scopeSha256 (kickoff/competition/toolchain.lock.json scope.scopeSha256); check-sequencing and authorize-implementation refuse any other. With B there is no approved competition scope and the lock cannot be committed.

requests.title: The competition's catalog verification contract (successor of ODR-R10-03 and ODR-R10-04)
requests.question: Adopt kickoff/competition/catalog-verification-contract.json as the contract a governed catalog verdict must bind in the competition? It is Rehearsal 010's contract (ODR-R10-03, ODR-R10-04; APR-R10-OWNER-2, 3d587618...) with only the catalog digest moved to the catalog ratified for v4.1.6 (0536ad29..., ODR-V416-CAT): the same governed producer, the same fault-sensitive content-round-trip category, the probe specification required, and the fact domain-profile-selected = false (INV-003 not applicable). Rehearsal 010's contract still pins the earlier catalog (7e5e8a40...), so a competition gate judged by it would refuse every verdict.
options: A: adopt the successor contract as shown
B: keep Rehearsal 010's contract (the governed catalog verdict refuses the v4.1.6 catalog)
requests.recommendation: A: the only change is the catalog the owner already ratified (ODR-V416-CAT).
requests.rationale: The contract is a governed asset; only the owner approves it (as ODR-R10-03).
requests.impact: The competition lock pins this file's sha256 as catalogVerification.contractSha256.

requests.title: Commit the competition toolchain lock (as ODR-RG-04)
requests.question: Adopt kickoff/competition/toolchain.lock.proposed.json as the competition's lock: v4.1.6 (tag indy-init-requirements-v4.1.6 at 2380b3d, manifest 8d3706d9...), the competition scope (ODR-COMP-SCOPE's scopeSha256), Conditor v0.10.21 (ODR-COMP-P14 A, all eight artifact digests as in its release checksums.txt), causa-storage-v1.1.0 (causa-data 7e10394), the competition repository kemiller2002/causa (pre-created, ODR-COMP-P07 A), the catalog verification contract (ODR-COMP-CATALOG-CONTRACT), the successor dependency lock (ODR-COMP-P15), the competition assertion merge needs (ODR-COMP-P16) and the competition process-evidence rules (ODR-COMP-P17: Rehearsal 010's with repository causa-t0), and, unchanged from Rehearsal 010's lock, echelon-current 1.37.0, the workstation target, the process-evidence plan, the design contract, the deadline policy, the journey bindings and the isolated test repository? Then commit it yourself as kickoff/competition/toolchain.lock.json, changing only `status` (to your pin) and `indyInit.commit` (to the merge commit of the pull request that adds this lock, or a later main commit you name).
options: A: adopt the proposed lock and commit it as kickoff/competition/toolchain.lock.json
B: keep the Rehearsal 010 lock (v4.1.5, the 37-item Legacy scope, Conditor v0.10.20)
requests.recommendation: A, after ODR-COMP-SCOPE, ODR-COMP-CATALOG-CONTRACT, ODR-COMP-P15, ODR-COMP-P16 and ODR-COMP-P17 are recorded (the lock pins their files' digests) and the live-provider preflight has run on the merged main. ODR-COMP-P12 A asks for exactly this re-pin.
requests.rationale: The lock is the one starting point every agent uses; only the owner commits it (ODR-RG-04). Recording this decision pins the proposed file you approved; your commit of toolchain.lock.json is the pin itself.
requests.impact: With B the competition runs on v4.1.5, the old scope and a Conditor without forma-workflow in its preset.
